subject: Information Theory
title: Kolmogorov Complexity
description: A quick, practical guide to Kolmogorov Complexity.

hook.text: The string '010101…' repeated 1,000 times is simple. A random 1,000-bit string is complex. Kolmogorov measured this.

buildup.text: Kolmogorov complexity: the length of the shortest program that produces the string.

discovery.text: A patterned string has low complexity—a short loop generates it. Random strings need programs as long as themselves.

twist.text: Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable. You can't write a program that calculates it for arbitrary strings.

climax.text: Despite being uncomputable, it's deeply useful as a theoretical benchmark for randomness and compression.

punchline.text: True complexity: the shortest description. Unmeasurable but real.

quiz.question: What is Kolmogorov complexity?
options: The file size of compressed data
The length of the shortest program producing the string
